repair_control_successor_rule: Return to the current canonical owner control record after 001C closure; do not invent A01-CLOSED-LOOP-REPAIR-001D unless a newer durable authority record explicitly declares it.
startup_sequence: Read this file from current main.
Read SYSTEM-TOPOLOGY-002.json and resolve the requested work to SYSTEM_MASTER/CORE, SYSTEM_MASTER/LEARNING, SYSTEM_MASTER/BOOK, SYSTEM_MASTER/BOOK/PROSE, shared infrastructure, or UNALLOCATED.
Fetch the live canonical control_ref for the owning system; never infer the live head from a chat, branch timestamp or checkpoint.
Read the owner's current control/state record selected on that live head.
Compare the live head/current state with the last sealed state checkpoint. If it moved, classify AUTHORITY_DELTA and reconcile only the delta before making current-state claims.
Check COMPLETION-LEDGER-001 before repeating work, WORK-OBLIGATION-REGISTRY-001 before selecting what is still owed, and EXPECTATION-REGISTRY-001 before declaring scope complete.

Read REPAIR-INBOX-REGISTRY-001, REPAIR-LEDGER-REGISTRY-001 and this lane's repair inbox before selecting unrelated new work. Revalidate any active repair transaction against current owner state and preserve its append-only event lineage.
Check the latest System State Reconciler standing when making repository-wide control claims. A red reconciler is a drift signal to adjudicate, not permission to ignore current owner state.
For repository-wide reconciliation, read active_census and resume at the first incomplete phase rather than restarting the audit.

If work is being delegated to Second Shift, read SECOND-SHIFT-EXECUTION-CONTROL-001, SECOND-SHIFT-DELEGATION-SCHEMA-002, the owner delegation file and the current per-lane shift event ledger; revalidate the delegation against the live control head and any live claim/lease immediately before admission/execution.

For mutation-capable Second Shift work, assume at-least-once invocation: bind a durable idempotency key, prevent overlapping live claims, checkpoint progress, classify/bound retries, and record timestamped state events. A READY successor left undispatched across an eligible worker cadence, a stale claim left unrecovered, or empty state without all-eight-rungs exhaustion is a control defect.

If an executable qualification fails, classify it before repair. A gateway non-PASS is brokered into a durable transaction after the gateway run; repair-eligible product failures emit an owner-worker dispatch packet. A changed repair candidate may emit a replacement A-01 return ticket only after deterministic prequalification PASS on the same exact replacement SHA.

For repair-control work, treat A01-CLOSED-LOOP-REPAIR-001B and A01-CLOSED-LOOP-REPAIR-001C as closed to their declared boundaries. Read the 001C closure and return to the current canonical owner control record rather than replaying 001C or inventing 001D.

For any future replacement or same-SHA repair retry, enter through the canonical repair-rerun workflow using the existing durable transaction_id. The gateway validates transaction/qualification/workstream/subject/ref binding and must not invoke the initial Repair Broker for a rerun.

A replacement A-01 result is adjudicated back into the same transaction. Only a real authoritative A-01 PASS receipt closes that transaction as PASS; hosted selftests prove control logic only. Subject failure re-dispatches the same transaction within remaining product-repair budget; infrastructure failure may receive one same-SHA retry; admission/dependency/control-plane/non-automatable outcomes retain truthful routes.

truth_classes.AUTHORITY_CURRENT: Owner, live control head, current state and evidence agree.
truth_classes.AUTHORITY_DELTA: Live owner control head/state moved after the last sealed checkpoint; read and reconcile only the delta before continuation.
truth_classes.UNALLOCATED: Work cannot be mapped to a current owner path; inspection is allowed, execution/promotion/scheduling is not.
truth_classes.STALE_DELEGATION: Second Shift delegation does not match the live owner control head or current open objective; do not execute.
truth_classes.READY_UNDISPATCHED: A current READY Second Shift delegation remained unclaimed across its next eligible owner-worker cadence without a live platform delay or claim; reconcile as a scope/control defect rather than accepting idle.
truth_classes.STALE_CLAIM: A Second Shift claim/lease expired or stopped heartbeating without terminal reconciliation; recover from the last durable checkpoint after live-authority revalidation.
truth_classes.FALSE_EMPTY: A Second Shift lane was treated as empty/idle without a current all-eight-rungs-exhausted proof; re-run the work-ahead ladder and bind independent safe work when available.
truth_classes.EVIDENCE_MISMATCH: Claimed standing exceeds or conflicts with exact receipt/artifact/subject evidence; fail closed and adjudicate.
truth_classes.REGISTERED_EXECUTABLE_MISSING: A control-plane-source qualification points to repository-owned executable bytes that are absent from the current control-plane checkout, or a subject-source qualification is absent on its exact subject checkout; fail closed at the correct authority boundary.
truth_classes.REPAIR_REQUEST_READY: An authoritative repairable subject failure has a durable owner-lane repair transaction and owner-worker dispatch packet; it may be reproduced/minimally repaired without granting PASS.
truth_classes.A01_REQUEUE_READY: A changed repair candidate has deterministic prequalification PASS on the same exact SHA and a durable replacement return ticket may enter canonical A-01 admission; it is not an authoritative PASS.
truth_classes.RETRY_REQUEST_READY: A prior replacement A-01 attempt encountered a bounded infrastructure failure and the same exact subject may be retried once through canonical A-01 without consuming another product-repair attempt.
truth_classes.REPAIR_OWNER_MISMATCH: A repair transaction no longer maps truthfully to the canonical owner/workstream; mutation/requeue is blocked until reconciled.

anti_surprise_invariant: No worker may say it is surprised by repository standing after beginning execution. Repository standing, active repair transactions, live delegation/claim standing and Second Shift execution state must be resolved before execution; a discovered mismatch becomes AUTHORITY_DELTA, EVIDENCE_MISMATCH, REPAIR_OWNER_MISMATCH, STALE_DELEGATION, READY_UNDISPATCHED, STALE_CLAIM or FALSE_EMPTY and is reconciled first.
write_rules: Historical evidence and completed exact-SHA receipts are append-only; do not rewrite them to match new taxonomy.
Open work belongs in the obligation registry with one owner; completion moves to evidence/completion history rather than disappearing.
Repository-wide censuses are checkpointed and resumable; never rebuild completed phases merely because a chat ended.
Current-control changes occur in the owning system lane; product-root governance selects/routes them but does not silently edit child objectives.
Any new first-class system or parent relationship requires a superseding topology ADR and topology registry version.
Any new workstream or qualification lane must resolve to an owner before execution.
Any Second Shift item must be removed from active delegation when completed/superseded and replaced only after a fresh owner re-evaluation.

Second Shift mutation work uses one owner-lane claim/lease, durable idempotency, checkpointed progress and bounded retry semantics. Completion/material block and successor binding are one logical reconciliation while time remains.
Second Shift time-state claims come from per-lane utilization events; commit spacing, workflow duration and runner uptime are not productivity evidence.

Second Shift IDLE is valid only with a current all-eight-rungs-exhausted proof. A stale/missing delegation, blocked path, unavailable A-01/runner, transient dependency or completed assignment never proves lane exhaustion.
An authoritative repairable failure creates a durable owner-lane repair transaction and append-only repair events; it may not exist only in chat memory.

A closed-loop repair that changes subject bytes creates a new exact SHA, deterministic prequalification evidence on that exact SHA, and a replacement A-01 request linked to the original failed receipt.

A replacement A-01 rerun never opens a second repair transaction for the same lineage; its receipt/attempt evidence is appended to the existing transaction and terminal or continuation state is derived there.
Repair Broker, repair worker, hosted tests and owner chats never grant A-01 PASS, promotion, publication or production authority.
